findings.title: average() panics with divide-by-zero on empty input

findings.body:
The empty-slice guard was removed. With samples empty, total is 0 and samples.len() as u32 is 0, so the expression total / 0 is an integer division by zero, which panics in Rust in both debug and release builds. The doc comment on line 1 says the function returns 0 when there are no samples.

Trigger: Calling average(&[]), or any path that passes an empty slice of samples.

Impact: Any caller that passes an empty slice, which the documented contract explicitly allows, panics instead of getting 0. This is a crash for callers of a public function.
findings.suggestion: Restore the guard: if samples.is_empty() { return 0; } before the division.
findings.title: average panics on empty input (division by zero)

risk_level.reason: Removing the empty-slice guard makes average panic with division by zero on empty input, contradicting the documented return of 0.
